div.p: A Feedback Control approach of Deadline Assignment (FC-DA) is developed to adjust control tasks' deadlines online thus to reduce output jitter. The feedback controller employs proportional law, whose parameter is adjusted adaptively to satisfy the total task set schedulability dynamically. The control algorithm is formulized as a deadline assignment expression. Simulations results illustrate that output jitter is reduced and control performance is improved greatly by the FC-DA.

div.head: Introduction
div.p: Real-time control systems are often implemented on a real-time kernel, in which multiple tasks compete for limited shared resources, such as processor time. So the primary goal of the real-time systems is to schedule processor time to these tasks to meet the timing constraints of the individual tasks. In control applications, closed-loop control tasks are often jitter-sensitive, especially when their periods are very short and processor utilization is high. In fact, the reduction of jitter is the secondary important goal of scheduling algorithm in real-time control systems.

A control task generally consists of three main parts: input data collection, control algorithm computation, and output signal transmission. From the control-theoretic perspective, it is useful to distinguish between sampling jitter (variation in the input instant) and output jitter. If AD converting is time-triggered and is not included in the body of control tasks, sampling can be regarded as jitter-free. Then, output jitter, i.e., time varying of response times, is mainly considered.

In [1], a straight and effective method to reduce output jitter is presented that assigns tighter deadlines to tasks rather than looking the tasks' deadlines as the same as their periods, and then schedules tasks based on their deadlines. Although shorter deadline is beneficial to control task to obtain higher priority, it impairs the schedulability of the entire task set. For this reason, a linear programming assignment with an objective function under schedulability constraint is presented in [2]. But the assignments of deadlines in both works are offline and static, which makes it difficult to be applied since the coexistence of various types of tasks and constraints makes the systems more complex and dynamic in nature. Using feedback scheduling [3], it is possible to do this assignment online.

In this paper, a Feedback Control approach of Deadline Assignment (FC-DA) is developed to adjust control tasks' deadlines online thus to reduce output jitter. Proportional control law is used in the FC-DA, whose parameter is adjusted adaptively to satisfy the total task set schedulability dynamically. The relationship between processor utilization and deadline assignment is formulized and embedded in the parameter of control law. Simulations results illustrate that output jitter is reduced and control performance is improved greatly by the FC-DA.

div.p: The research of this work is restricted to the preemptive, uniprocessor environment. And the basic scheduling algorithm is Earliest Deadline First (EDF) [4], which dynamically assigns a higher priority to the task with earlier deadline, and is known to be optimal in the sense of feasibility.

The FC-DA is mainly composed of a PID controller. Feedback information of processor utilization and controlled variable (jitter) are collected periodically, similar as sensors in the control system. The controller uses PID algorithm to compute control output according to the difference between jitter setting point and corresponding controlled variable. The PID controller's output is the relative deadlines of control tasks.

Moreover, adaptive technique is used in this controller through the measurement of processor utilization to guarantee the schedulability of the entire task set. Note that the processor is not at all times fully loaded, i.e., there exists various residual processor' power at runtime. So we can confine the extra processor resources owing to the decrease of deadlines to these residues through measuring processor utilization online. This character is used for the proportional controller factor self-tuning in our feedback scheduling as shown in Fig. 1.

div.head: Discussion
div.p: As shown in Fig. 1, the disturbance of dynamical workload enters the system locally in a well-defined way. The measured variable, i.e., output jitter, is influenced by the disturbance, and the control variable, i.e., output of the controller, enters the system in the neighborhood of the disturbance. Thus, the feedback architecture can reduce the effect of the disturbance entering the system. According to control theory, this approach is simple and effective because it is not necessary to have detailed information about the characteristics of the scheduling process, which is a challenge problem still. Further, note that a high gain, i.e., a smaller value of β in Fig. 3, is preferable for reducing the disturbance.

When the utilization raises dynamically, the value of decreases, i.e., the range of adjustable relative deadline is narrowed. So the schedulability constraint transfers from line to line first. Then, the transient behavior of the system moves along line . Finally, the system is stabilized at new equilibrium point .

div.p: The simulation experiments are based on TrueTime kernel [6], which is developed as a toolbox for Matlab. To illustrate how the online deadline assignment improves the control performance, simulations have been carried out on three identical servomotors. The FC-DA itself executes as a periodic task in TrueTime kernel, and its period is chosen as 50ms. The servomotors are given with square-wave reference input. The first type of simulations is conducted to obtain the normal responses of servomotors when there are only three closed-loop tasks scheduled under basic EDF algorithm in the kernel. div.p: The second type of simulations is conducted to show how the control performance is damaged when suffering from the disturbance coming from aperiodic tasks. At the beginning time of 0~200ms, a set of sporadic tasks are generated whose mean execution time are all assumed to be 0.2ms, and period are randomly taken from the interval (4ms, 10ms). At the beginning phase, the measurements show that processor utilization is 79.6% and output jitter is 0.729, i.e., 24.3% for each task. The responses of the servomotors are shown in Fig. 5. It can be seen that the control performances are damaged in different degree. The last type of simulations is conducted to illustrate that the FC-DA improves the control performance through online deadline assignment. The components of task set are the same as that of the second simulation. But the FC-DA is used to assign the deadlines for the three control tasks. The simulation results are shown in Fig. 6. And the measured 1. It is seen that the control performance is improved greatly by the FC-DA compared with that of basic EDF algorithm. The output jitter in the transient process is reduced rapidly because of feedback control. After the fifth period, the measured output jitter is nearly zero again since the disturbance is deleted.

div.head: Conclusions
div.p: This paper presents a feedback control approach to reduce the closed-loop control tasks' output jitter through online adjusting their relative deadlines. To satisfy the schedulability of task set, adaptive technique is used to confine the extra processor consumption owing to the decrease of deadlines to variable utilization residue, which is implemented by control parameter self-tuning. The feedback controller is formulized as deadline assignment expression. Simulation results illustrate that output jitter is reduced and control performance is improved greatly.
